After: only edge 5 is gone, shown dashed, while its parallel twin, edge 1, remains." width="100%"} Removes an edge directly using its unique edge identifier. This is more efficient than deleting by source and target nodes when the edge ID is known, and is particularly useful for multigraphs where multiple edges may exist between the same pair of nodes. Only the edge is removed; its endpoint nodes stay in the graph. Edge IDs are assigned automatically when edges are created and can be found with `get_edge_ids()`, `find_edge_ids()` (all edges between two nodes), selection helpers such as `get_selected_edge_ids()`, or the `id` column of `get_edge_df()`. The graph is modified in place and the deletion is recorded in the step log (see `steps`). It behaves the same as `delete_edge(id=...)`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The unique integer identifier of the edge to remove. Must refer to an edge that currently exists; IDs of previously deleted edges are not reused. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [EdgeNotFoundError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If no edge exists with the specified ID. It is a subclass of both `KeyError` and `ValueError`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `delete_edge_by_id()` removes a single edge directly, without resolving source and target nodes first: ::: {#f13ebe8e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) edge_id = graph.get_edge_ids()[0] graph.delete_edge_by_id(edge_id=edge_id) graph.has_edge(source="A", target="B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` False ``` ::: ::: That makes it the right tool for multigraphs, where several edges connect the same pair of nodes and only a specific one should be removed. `find_edge_ids()` lists the parallel edges, and deleting the second one leaves the weight `1.0` edge in place: ::: {#a85f4610 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.0) .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=2.0) ) parallel = graph.find_edge_ids("A", "B") graph.delete_edge_by_id(edge_id=parallel[1]) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
